enrichment.sped_program_notes: No SPED program in the K-12/IDEA sense. Any disability services would be a college ADA/504 office, not a Special Education department with IEP caseloads.
enrichment.region_context: Colorado-based post-secondary institution. Community colleges in Colorado fall under the Colorado Community College System (CCCS), not a K-12 district governance structure, and are not subject to IDEA mandates.
enrichment.pain_points: Not applicable — post-secondary institutions do not operate under IDEA and do not manage IEPs. Disability accommodations at this level are governed by ADA/Section 504, outside Journify's scope.
enrichment.fit_reasoning: Hard disqualifier: "Rocky Mountain Community College" is almost certainly a post-secondary institution, not a K-12 public school district. The intake notes themselves flag this ("may not be K-12"). Journify Learning is purpose-built for K-12 SPED teams (IEP drafting, goal tracking, IDEA compliance) and has no product-market fit with higher education. Even if the college has a disability services office, it operates under ADA/Section 504 — not IDEA — and would not use IEP workflows. Zero intent signals further confirm no engagement from a SPED decision-maker. Score: 0.
